title: A 0.9pJ/b 108Gb/s PAM-4 VCSEL-Based Direct-Drive Optical Engine
problem: Electrical interconnects for high-throughput data centers face scalability limits due to power-hungry equalization and DSP; pluggable optical modules add re-timer complexity and latency; co-packaged optics (CPO) requires efficient direct-drive without DSP re-timing.
motivation: Data center bandwidth demands exceed electrical interconnect capabilities; eliminating re-timers in CPO enables lower latency and power, but requires high-linearity optical circuits tolerating complex channel imperfections.
method: The system connects a laser with four-level modulation (VCSEL-PAM-4) directly to a receiver amplifier without adding digital processing delays. It uses an analog equalizer circuit (CZ-CTIE, which uses coupled inductors) embedded in the laser driver to fix signal distortion from the laser's frequency response, and a high-linearity amplifier that converts optical to electrical signals while another equalizer stage in the amplifier's feedback corrects remaining distortion. This approach lets the receiver decode data at 108 Gb/s with minimal power overhead by avoiding digital re-timing.
key_novelty: Using a continuous-time analog equalizer circuit (CZ-CTIE) embedded in the optical driver and receiver to fix signal distortion eliminates the power-hungry digital re-processing step normally required for direct-drive optical signals.
contributions: Complex-zero CTIE equalization for VCSEL response
limitations: Abstract-only; bit error rate, optical power budget, reach distance, temperature stability, and cost comparison not discussed.
primary_theme: Direct-drive PAM-4 optical engine for co-packaged optics
